headline: Roman had a fall on 2026-10-19, then new evening confusion (including a stove left on) and 8.6% weight loss since 09-05. His ADL needs have also increased, and the notes conflict on whether the fall is resolved.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Roman was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or visit are documented after 11-09.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11-09 nursing note. The statement that no results or visit are documented after 11-09 is consistent with the cited note and the empty encounters record.

items.statement: Roman fell at home in the kitchen on 2026-10-19 while reaching for a cabinet. He had a left forearm skin tear and denied head strike or loss of consciousness. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. On 10-24 PT found his gait slow and unsteady (Timed Up and Go 19 s), recommended a front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and planned twice-weekly PT.
items.verifier_note: Details match notes n001 and n002: kitchen fall, left forearm skin tear, no head strike or LOC, high fall risk, PT referral. PT on 10-24 found slow unsteady gait, TUG 19 s, and recommended a walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars, with twice-weekly PT.

items.statement: Documentation conflict: a second PT note dated 2026-10-24 calls the fall resolved, says he is at baseline, and removes it from the active problem list. The PT evaluation the same day found unsteady gait and set up ongoing therapy and equipment recommendations. The team should confirm the fall-risk status.
items.verifier_note: Note n016 dated 10-24 says the fall is resolved, at baseline, and removed from the problem list. Note n002 the same day documents unsteady gait and ongoing PT. The conflict is accurately described.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 11-24 (−7.1 kg, −8.6%), declining at each reading (79.8 kg on 10-01, 77.3 kg on 10-28). On 11-24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: Weights, change (-7.1 kg, -8.6%) and the intermediate readings match the vitals record. The dietitian note supports poor appetite, skipped breakfast, 50% of lunches eaten, and the plan of supplement twice daily, weekly weights and dental check. The note's '9%' is a rounding of 8.6%.

items.statement: On 2026-09-18 the home care aide reported that Roman needed hands-on help out of the tub and was skipping showers for fear of slipping. On 09-25 OT found he needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing (independent at last review). OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing. The notes do not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: Both notes match: the 09-18 aide report, the 09-25 OT moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing (previously independent), and the three recommendations. The notes do not show implementation, as the statement says.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 11-09 completed, and what did they show?
Is the fall from 10-19 resolved or still active, given the PT evaluation of 10-24 and the conflicting PT note? Should the problem list be corrected?
Have the walker, grab bars, tub transfer bench, handheld shower and extra bathing hours been arranged?
Is it safe for Roman to be alone at home given the evening confusion and the stove incident? What support does Linda need?
Naproxen is still on his active medication list. Should it be covered in the medication review given the recent changes?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and readmissions, with reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls and near-falls: count and characterize any falls in the window, including injuries and fall-risk screening. Note fall risk from chronic knee osteoarthritis, low back pain, fibromyalgia, and any sedating or BP-lowering medications.

Medication changes since last review: list every start, stop, and dose change against the active list (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, naproxen, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin). Flag any new NSAID or antiplatelet use alongside clopidogrel and naproxen, since bleeding and GI risk and renal effects are relevant, and reconcile any PRN or OTC analgesic use.

Cardiac and BP review: blood pressure readings trend (hypotension or orthostatic symptoms on metoprolol, hypertension control), chest pain or nitroglycerin use frequency, angina symptoms, heart rate, and any cardiology follow-up or lipid results on simvastatin.
Respiratory status: COPD/chronic bronchitis symptoms, inhaler use or new respiratory prescriptions, oxygen saturation readings, exacerbations, and pulmonary-related encounters.
Anemia and bleeding: most recent hemoglobin/CBC trend, any bleeding or melena signs given clopidogrel plus naproxen, and whether iron studies or GI follow-up are pending.
Metabolic and weight trend: weight and BMI trend across the window (obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes), most recent HbA1c or glucose, and lipid panel status.
Renal and lab monitoring tied to NSAID use: creatinine, eGFR, potassium, and any lab orders due or overdue in the window.
Pain and function: chronic pain and fibromyalgia scores, pain-interference change, knee OA and back pain flare reports, ADL and IADL status, mobility aids, and any PT/OT referrals or completions.

Cognition, mood, and engagement: screen results (for example PHQ or GAD and any cognitive screen), depression or anxiety notes, PACE center attendance and missed days, transportation issues, and social isolation signals.

Caregiver and care-plan items: caregiver availability or changes, housing or safety concerns, advance directive and healthcare proxy status, care-plan goals and due reassessments (MDS or interdisciplinary assessment due dates), and any open action items from the last IDT meeting. Note the enrollment date (2024-10-07) and confirm the care plan was updated in the last 12 months.
